name: pipeline-ordering
description: Tests whether the model places sampling first in the pipeline (before formatting)
prompt: Set up a slog pipeline in Go using samber/slog libraries with PII scrubbing (mask email fields), error routing to Sentry, and log sampling at 10%. Show the complete handler composition using slog-multi, slog-sampling, and slog-formatter.
trap: Without the skill, the model places sampling last (after formatting) or in the middle, wasting CPU on records that get dropped

assertions.text: Sampling occurs early on sampled branches; routing may precede it to exempt errors
Uses slog-sampling library (slogsampling) for sampling, not custom code
Uses slog-formatter for PII scrubbing (PIIFormatter or FormatByKey)
Uses slogmulti.Router or Fanout for routing to Sentry
Explains or demonstrates why sampling should be first (avoid wasted CPU on dropped records)

name: router-firstmatch-vs-router-all-matches
description: Tests whether the model distinguishes Router (all matching) from Router+FirstMatch (first match only)
prompt: I have a slog-multi Router with two rules: (1) ERROR and above → PagerDuty, (2) WARN and above → Slack. My problem: ERROR logs are going to BOTH PagerDuty AND Slack. I only want errors in PagerDuty, not duplicated in Slack. How do I fix this with slog-multi?
trap: Without the skill, the model adds a LevelIs(slog.LevelWarn) predicate to the Slack handler thinking that fixes it — LevelIs matches exactly WARN, which actually excludes ERROR; threshold predicates need explicit comparisons. The correct fix is Router().Add(...).FirstMatch() so routing stops at the first matching handler.

assertions.text: Identifies that the default Router sends to ALL matching handlers (both Slack and PagerDuty match for ERROR)
Recommends using .FirstMatch() on the Router to stop at the first matching handler
Recognizes LevelIs(Warn) is exact; either disjoint predicates or FirstMatch with descending threshold rules avoids duplicates
Shows descending >=Error and >=Warn predicates with FirstMatch, or correctly explains disjoint exact-level routing
Explains the semantic difference: Router routes to ALL matches, FirstMatch routes to FIRST match only

name: missing-close-batch
description: Tests whether the model remembers to call Close() on batch handlers
prompt: Set up slog to send logs to Datadog using samber/slog-datadog in a Go HTTP server with graceful shutdown. Show the complete main() function.
trap: Without the skill, the model forgets to close the handler on shutdown, causing buffered logs to be lost

assertions.text: Calls handler.Stop(ctx) or defer handler.Stop(ctx) for the Datadog handler (not Close)
Uses Option{}.NewDatadogHandler() constructor pattern
Close happens during graceful shutdown (signal handling or defer in main)
Supplies the required Datadog client and explicitly enables Batching when showing buffered delivery; calls Stop on shutdown
Import path is github.com/samber/slog-datadog/v2 or later

name: sampling-matcher-grouping
description: Tests whether the model understands slog-sampling Matchers for deduplication grouping
prompt: I've set up ThresholdSamplingOption in my Go service: log the first 10 per 5s, then sample at 10%. It works, but I notice that 'user not found' (DEBUG) and 'cache miss' (DEBUG) are being counted together in the same bucket. After 10 total DEBUG logs from both messages, both get sampled. I want each distinct log message to have its own counter of 10. How do I fix this with samber/slog-sampling?
trap: Without the skill, the model either rebuilds sampling from scratch or suggests separate logger instances per message. The default is already level+message; after checking for a custom grouping override, set the Matcher to MatchByLevelAndMessage() (or MatchByMessage()) so each unique message gets its own deduplication bucket instead of all records sharing one bucket.

assertions.text: Recognizes MatchByLevelAndMessage is already the default; checks whether a custom matcher such as MatchByLevel was configured
Recommends setting the Matcher field on ThresholdSamplingOption to MatchByLevelAndMessage() or MatchByMessage()
Explains that each unique message will then have its own independent threshold counter
Does NOT suggest creating separate logger instances per message type as the solution
Does NOT suggest rewriting custom sampling logic outside of slog-sampling

name: router-warn-level-gap
description: Tests whether the model identifies that WARN records are silently dropped in a Router with only ERROR and INFO predicates
prompt:
I have this slog-multi Router setup. My ERROR logs reach Sentry, my INFO logs reach Loki, but my WARN logs are silently disappearing — they don't reach either handler. My global slog level is set to Debug so filtering isn't the issue. What's wrong?

```go
logger := slog.New(
    slogmulti.Router().
        Add(sentryHandler, slogmulti.LevelIs(slog.LevelError)).
        Add(lokiHandler, slogmulti.LevelIs(slog.LevelInfo)).
        Handler(),
)
```
trap: Without the skill, the model suspects Loki configuration, slog level filters, or assumes LevelIs(Info) includes Warn. The skill teaches that Router predicates are exact — LevelIs(Info) matches ONLY Info, not Warn or above. WARN records match no predicate and are silently dropped. Fix: add a catch-all handler or use a predicate that covers Warn.

assertions.text: Correctly identifies that LevelIs(slog.LevelInfo) matches ONLY Info level, not Warn
Explains that Router silently drops records that match no predicate
Does NOT suggest the global slog level or Loki configuration as the root cause
Proposes adding a catch-all handler (no predicate) or a LevelIs(slog.LevelWarn) rule to capture WARN records
Correctly explains that Router predicates are exact-level matches, not 'level and above'

name: http-middleware-error-level-differentiation
description: Tests whether the model uses slog-gin Config to log 4xx and 5xx at different levels instead of uniform INFO
prompt: I've added sloggin.NewWithConfig(logger, sloggin.Config{}) to my Gin server for request logging. My log aggregation tool shows that 404s and 500s both appear as INFO level, making it hard to alert on server errors. How do I make 4xx client errors log at WARN and 5xx server errors log at ERROR, while keeping normal requests at INFO, using samber/slog-gin?
trap: Without the skill, the model wraps sloggin in a custom middleware or post-processes log records to change the level. The skill teaches that slog-gin's Config struct has ClientErrorLevel and ServerErrorLevel fields that handle this natively — no custom middleware needed.

assertions.text: Uses explicit level fields in NewWithConfig or starts from DefaultConfig; New(logger) already uses differentiated levels
Sets ClientErrorLevel: slog.LevelWarn in the Config for 4xx responses
Sets ServerErrorLevel: slog.LevelError in the Config for 5xx responses
Sets DefaultLevel: slog.LevelInfo in the Config for 2xx/3xx responses
Does NOT implement a custom Gin middleware or post-processing logic to change log levels

name: pipe-middleware-chain
description: Tests whether the model uses Pipe middleware instead of custom Handler wrapper
prompt: I need to inject a trace_id from OpenTelemetry context and scrub email addresses from all log records before they reach any handler. I'm using samber/slog-multi. Show me how to set this up as reusable middleware.
trap: Without the skill, the model creates a custom slog.Handler wrapper struct instead of using slogmulti.Pipe with inline middleware

assertions.text: Uses slogmulti.Pipe() for middleware chaining
Creates middleware for trace_id injection (inline middleware or AttrFromContext)
Creates middleware or formatter for email/PII scrubbing
Pipe wraps the final sink handler(s)
Does NOT implement a custom slog.Handler struct with Enabled/Handle/WithAttrs/WithGroup methods

name: failover-handler
description: Tests whether the model uses Failover instead of custom retry logic
prompt: My slog pipeline sends logs to Loki over the network, but Loki has occasional outages lasting 1-5 minutes. I want to automatically fall back to local file logging when Loki is unavailable, then resume Loki when it's back. Show the setup using samber/slog-multi.
trap: Without the skill, the model builds custom retry/fallback logic with goroutines and channels instead of using slog-multi's Failover handler

assertions.text: Explains Failover responds only to returned Handle errors and cannot detect later buffered Loki delivery failures
Loki handler is the primary (first) handler in the Failover chain
File/local handler is the fallback (second) handler
Proposes durable local logging plus forwarding, or a handler whose synchronous error semantics meet the requirement
Does not promise that slog-loki enqueue success proves network delivery

name: pool-vs-fanout-latency
description: Tests the delivery and latency differences between Pool and Fanout
prompt: I'm replacing slogmulti.Fanout with slogmulti.Pool to reduce log-call latency. I have 4 handlers with these p99 write times: stdout (1ms), Loki (20ms), Datadog (30ms), Sentry (15ms). My current Fanout p99 latency per log call is ~66ms. What will Pool's p99 latency be, and are there any risks I should know about with Pool that don't exist with Fanout?
trap: Without the skill, the model says Pool will have ~0ms latency (wrongly treating it as fire-and-forget) or cannot identify the risks. The skill teaches: Pool selects one enabled handler, retrying sequentially on error. It no longer delivers every record to every sink, and marginal handler p99 values do not determine aggregate p99.

assertions.text: Does not infer aggregate p99 from marginal handler p99 values; describes selected-handler latency and sequential error retries
Explains Pool sends each record to one successful handler, not all handlers concurrently
Identifies the semantic change: each sink receives only a subset of records
Shows correct Pool syntax: slogmulti.Pool()(handlers...) with the double call
Does NOT claim Pool is fully asynchronous/fire-and-forget with zero latency impact

name: formatter-pii-scrubbing
description: Tests whether the model uses slog-formatter as Pipe middleware for cross-cutting PII scrubbing
prompt: I need to ensure no email addresses or IP addresses appear in any log output from my Go service. We use slog with slog-multi routing to 3 different handlers (stdout, Loki, Sentry). Show me how to add PII protection that applies to ALL handlers in one place.
trap: Without the skill, the model adds per-handler filtering or regex on output instead of using slog-formatter as a Pipe middleware wrapping all downstream handlers

assertions.text: Uses slog-formatter library (slogformatter package)
Explains selected-attribute masking does not guarantee no PII anywhere; covers message text and nested/error data according to a tested redaction policy
Applies formatter as a Pipe middleware wrapping all downstream handlers (not per-handler)
Formatter is applied once in the pipeline, before the Router/Fanout
Does not claim PIIFormatter detects every email/IP; prefers structured allowlisting/redaction with explicit coverage

name: backend-option-pattern
description: Tests whether the model uses correct Option{} constructor pattern for backend handlers
prompt: Set up slog to send error-level logs to Sentry and all logs to Grafana Loki using samber/slog-sentry and samber/slog-loki. Show the complete setup with correct imports and handler creation.
trap: Without the skill, the model uses incorrect constructor patterns (e.g., New() function, slogsentry.New(), or positional args) instead of the Option{}.NewXxxHandler() pattern

assertions.text: Uses slogsentry.Option{}.NewSentryHandler() constructor pattern
Uses slogloki.Option{}.NewLokiHandler() constructor pattern
Uses slogmulti.Router() for level-based routing (errors to Sentry, all to Loki)
Import paths use versioned modules (github.com/samber/slog-sentry/v2, github.com/samber/slog-loki/v3)
Calls lokiClient.Stop() or defer lokiClient.Stop() for graceful shutdown (flush buffered logs)

name: attrfromcontext-without-middleware
description: Tests matching context producers, extractor keys and context-aware logging calls
trap: Checks the actual context producer, matching key type, and context passed to the log call; an HTTP logging middleware is neither required nor sufficient by itself

assertions.text: Checks whether request_id is populated under the same key and whether the logging call receives that context
Populates the key in application code or middleware and calls InfoContext/ErrorContext
Explains that a context producer must set the requested value; that may be application code or middleware
Checks key identity/type and avoids unchecked type assertions
Shows matching value insertion and extraction and a context-aware log call
Does not assume WithRequestID populates an arbitrary string context key
Does not assume the cause without checking key identity and whether the log call passes the request context
